newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra alters media ownership for regionals.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra alters media ownership for regionals.

text.p: The Australian government reformed media ownership laws on Wednesday to allow a single licencee to own a newspaper and a radio station in the same area, in certain cases.

"The bill amends the Broadcasting Services Act to exclude newspapers with a circulaton of less than two percent of a commmercial radio broadcaster's licence area population from the cross media rules," Territories Minister Warwick Smith, representing Communications Minister Richard Alston in the lower house, told Parliament.

Smith said the amendment removed an unintended consequence of the rules which prevented smaller newspapers owning a commercial broadcasting licence if they had 50 percent of their circulation in the same area.
The rules were unrealistic where newspapers served regional areas in which populations were relatively small within wider commercial licence areas, he said.

Last year, authorities told Australian Provincial Newspapers it had breached cross-media limits when it bought radio station 4KQ, which broadcast into an area widely covered by the company's small Queensland Times newspaper in Ipswich, near the Queensland state capital of Brisbane.
The legislation is retroactive and does cover Australian Provincial Newspapers, a spokesman for Alston told Reuters.
